english: A tank initially contains $100$ litres of brine in which $2$ kg of salt is dissolved. Pure water flows into the tank at the rate of $1$ litre per minute, and the well-stirred mixture flows out at the rate of $2$ litres per minute. Then the amount of salt, in kg, in the tank at the instant when the tank contains $60$ litres of brine is ______.
hindi: एक टंकी में प्रारम्भ में $100$ लीटर लवण-जल है जिसमें $2$ kg लवण घुला है। टंकी में शुद्ध जल $1$ लीटर प्रति मिनट की दर से प्रवेश करता है तथा भली-भाँति मिश्रित घोल $2$ लीटर प्रति मिनट की दर से बाहर निकलता है। तब जिस क्षण टंकी में $60$ लीटर लवण-जल है, उस क्षण टंकी में लवण की मात्रा, kg में, ______ है।
solution_full: Let $S(t)$ kg be the salt and $V(t)$ litres the volume at time $t$ minutes. The net outflow is $1$ litre per minute, so $V=100-t$.
Pure water brings no salt; the outflow removes salt at the rate $2\cdot\dfrac{S}{V}$ kg per minute. So $\dfrac{dS}{dt}=-\dfrac{2S}{100-t}$, $0\le t<100$.
A constant-volume model would give the exponential $2e^{-2t/100}$ instead, a common error.
originality_note: New: a mixture problem in which the tank drains, so the salt is a power of the volume, S = S0 (V/V0)^2, rather than an exponential (way 4). Closest known: constant-volume brine tanks with exponential decay. Different because: the inflow and outflow rates differ, so the volume changes and the exponential is replaced by a power law.
blueprint_concepts: Application problems: growth, decay, Newton's law of cooling, mixtures

concept_use.Application problems: growth, decay, New: A mixture problem with a draining volume: the salt balance gives dS/dt = -2S/(100 - t), separated and integrated to S = 2(V/100)^2.
